circumcīdānĕus , a, um, adj. circumcīdo, prop.,
I.of or from cutting or paring around: “mustum,” wine pressed out after the ordinary pressing, when the husks and stems remaining in the press had been cut around, Cato, R. R. 23, 4 ; cf. Plin. 14, 20, 25, § 124 sq.; Col. 12, 36; “the same, called mustum circumcisicium or circumcisitum,” Varr. R. R. 1, 54, 3 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
